title: telemetry-bridge-concept-and-widget-sprint-canvas
content:
Purpose
This doc articulates a lightweight concept were calling the "telemetry bridge": a small set of stable, cross-layer signals and dashboard widgets that sit between low-level instrumentation (spans, k-v cache events, per-token stats) and operator-facing dashboards. Goal is to reduce investigation time for tenant-facing incidents and make rollout telemetry usable by non-infra teams.

Scope and intended outcomes
- Define a compact metric set (<= 12 signals) for the bridge that balances cost and actionability.
- Specify tracing anchor conventions to connect a bridge widget back to raw spans quickly.
- Draft a widget/mini-dashboard template for fast onboarding of new models and rollouts.
- Sprint canvas: a three-week plan to prototype widgets, instrument one model, and validate with an ops tabletop.

Audience
Primary: oncall engineers, SREs, and model rollout owners. Secondary: product owners and solutions engineers who need rapid incident context.

Principles and constraints
- Operator-first: widgets answer the question "what to do next"; they are not exhaustive telemetry surfaces.
- Cost-bounded: keep sample rates and retention conservative; prefer aggregated probes over full-span retention where possible.
- Traceable: every metric in the bridge must include a deterministic pointer to one or more trace-anchor tags (span_id, session_id, tenant_id).
- Stable semantics: avoid fields that frequently change across model versions (e.g., per-layer latencies) unless absolutely necessary.

Telemetry bridge metric set (compact definitions)
Each metric below includes: name | intent | owner | cardinality guidance | alerting suggestion
1) token-path-latency_p50_p95 | Intent: user-perceived latency for token generation end-to-end (frontend to last-token) | Owner: eng-sre | Cardinality: low (route/model buckets) | Alert: p95 > 350ms sustained 5m
2) prefix-kv-warmth | Intent: fraction of requests with a warm K/V cache hit for prefix tokens | Owner: serving-runtime | Cardinality: medium (tenant+model) | Alert: drop > 10pp baseline over 10m
3) batch-overhang-rate | Intent: pct of requests delayed by batching window beyond target latency | Owner: infra-serving | Cardinality: low | Alert: > 3% sustained 5m
4) model-variant-fallback-rate | Intent: percentage of requests routed to a fallback variant (quality or capacity) | Owner: routing | Cardinality: low | Alert: > 1% sustained or sudden spike
5) inference-error-rate | Intent: api-level error responses (5xx, rate-limit/exhaustion) normalized by token count | Owner: eng-sre | Cardinality: low | Alert: > 0.5% increase vs baseline
6) enqueue-time_p99 | Intent: tail queuing delay before the request is scheduled on GPU | Owner: serving-runtime | Cardinality: low | Alert: p99 > 200ms
7) kv-eviction-pressure | Intent: eviction events per minute for shared kv caches | Owner: platform-engineering | Cardinality: low | Alert: sustained increase > 2x baseline
8) tenant-cold-hit-fraction | Intent: fraction of that tenant's requests that observe model cold-start behaviors | Owner: solutions-engineering | Cardinality: medium | Alert: tenant-specific SLA breach threshold
9) streaming-churn-index | Intent: rate of mid-stream reconnects or early-client-aborts | Owner: console-and-tooling | Cardinality: low | Alert: > 0.3% for routes with streaming enabled
10) perplexity-regression-probe | Intent: spot-check average perplexity for a curated prompt set during rollouts | Owner: applied-ml | Cardinality: low | Alert: target delta > configured threshold
11) tail-token-cost | Intent: tokens-per-session p95 (cost signal) | Owner: finance-and-legal (billing liaison) | Cardinality: low | Alert: unexplained jump in p95 tokens/session
12) span-linked-sample-rate | Intent: fraction of requests with a full trace attached (for forensic debugging) | Owner: observability | Cardinality: low | Alert: < configured minimum (ensures sample coverage)

Trace anchor conventions (how to map bridge metrics back to spans)
- All bridge metrics MUST surface a canonical trace_anchor tag: "trace_anchor_id". This tag is a deterministic composite: {tenant_id}:{route_id}:{request_id_short} where request_id_short is first 8 chars of request_id.
- When a bridge widget shows a suspicious cohort (e.g., tenant X in the last 5m), operators can click "open traces" to run a filtered trace query for trace_anchor_id prefix.
- For latency investigations, we attach span annotations: "kvcache:hit|miss", "batch:delayed", "variant:fallback". These should be present on the server-side request span.

Widget / mini-dashboard template (operator flow first)
Top row (incident triage):
- Single line summary: tokens/sec, aggregated p95 lat, error-rate, fallback-rate (sparklines, 15m/1h/24h).
- Heatmap: tenant-weighted p95 latency by route (top 20 tenants).

Middle row (forensic quicklinks):
- Bridge metric detail panels (prefix-kv-warmth, enqueue-time_p99, batch-overhang-rate). Each panel includes a "show traces" action that opens a pre-populated trace query using the trace_anchor_id filter.
- Recent rollout flag timeline (canary % changes and associated commits).

Bottom row (ops playbook + next actions):
- Top 3 likely root causes (auto-suggested via a simple heuristic: if kv-warmth drops and enqueue time climbs -> recommend "kv-prefetch heatup").
- Quick remediation buttons for ops (re-task prefetch, pin older model variant, scale-queue).

Onboarding checklist for a new model/service to be covered by bridge widgets
- Instrumentation: ensure server-side spans include trace_anchor_id and kvcache annotations.
- Metric hooks: export prefix-kv-warmth and enqueue-time at route granularity.
- Dashboard: add the model to the mini-dashboard template and configure tenant-tiling parameters.
- Tabletop: run a synthetic incident drill (2h) with ops and model owner using the synthetic probe harness.

Sprint canvas (3-week prototype plan)
Week 1: implement metric plumbing for 4 metrics (token-path-latency, prefix-kv-warmth, enqueue-time_p99, model-variant-fallback-rate) for one model. Build bridge aggregation job and store short retention aggregates.
Week 2: build mini-dashboard template and trace-open links. Run internal tabletop incident using synthetic probe and record investigation time.
Week 3: iterate alerts and add 2 extra metrics (kv-eviction-pressure, batch-overhang-rate). Finalize onboarding checklist and capture a runbook stub for the model.

Success criteria (how we judge prototype)
- Mean time to map from bridge alert to relevant spans reduces by >= 40% in the tabletop drill.
- Bridge metric set catches at least 80% of simulated incidents in the tabletop (kvcache misses, batch delays, routing fallbacks).
- Dashboard query cost under target budget for 30-day retention.

Open questions / risks
- Cardinality leakage: tenant+model tags could produce high-cardinality heat. Mitigation: tiered retention and coarse-grain aggregation for older windows.
- Owner bandwidth: who will maintain the bridge aggregation job long-term? Proposal: observability owns infra; serving-runtime owns model-specific annotations.
- Remediation actions integration: exposing remediation buttons could be risky; start with read-only guidance and manual ops playbook links.

Immediate next steps (owner-assigned)
- Jordan Kim: finalize trace_anchor_id format and post to Confluence (due 2026-01-22).
- Avery Patel: prototype aggregation job for prefix-kv-warmth for test-model-1 (due 2026-01-29).
- Maya Rodriguez: wire a basic mini-dashboard layout in Grafana and add synthetic probes (due 2026-02-05).
- Samir Gupta: draft tabletop script and incident scenarios (due 2026-02-09).

Appendix: quick heuristics for "what this metric tells you"
- If prefix-kv-warmth drops and enqueue-time rises: prioritize prefetching heuristics or cache sizing.
- If batch-overhang-rate spikes but token-path-latency p50 stays: indicates batching window skew; check scheduling/packing changes.
- If fallback-rate increases with normal errors: likely model rollout or capacity pressure; check routing policies and rollout controls.

Notes: this doc is intentionally prescriptive but small in scope. The goal for the prototype is to show measurable ops value and a clear migration path to broader coverage.

End of doc.
